A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CARSO and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–F. Retained material can be reliably matched despite reformatting and the added aggregation experiment.

before.justification: v4 reports original clean and adversarial classification results in Tables 2–3, plus preliminary purifier-training findings in Appendix C.

after.justification: v5 retains these original results and adds an experimental comparison of aggregation strategies in Appendix D.2 and Table 4.

M1.justification: The classifier, representation-conditioned VAE, hierarchical encoders, balanced training batches, and normalized doubly-exponential aggregation rule are retained. Appendix E's architectures also match. The new aggregation experiment evaluates alternatives without changing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and TinyImageNet-200, and retain the preliminary MNIST and Fashion-MNIST studies in Appendix C. The new aggregation ablation reuses existing CIFAR tasks and threat conditions.

E2.justification: Section 5.2 replaces the CIFAR-10 best adversarial-training comparator, Peng et al.'s RAWideResNet-70-16, with Bartoldson et al.'s WideResNet-96-16. Table 4 newly evaluates logit and probability averaging. Appendix F still attributes the CIFAR-10 best comparator to Cui et al., inconsistently with the updated main text.

E3.justification: The reported CIFAR-100 learning-rate annealing duration changes from 250 epochs in v4 Table 14 to 150 in v5 Table 15, consistent with the stated 200-epoch total; this does not establish that training was rerun. The new aggregation ablation holds Section 5's other conditions fixed. The randAA and PGD+EoT protocols are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.2 and Table 4 directly test the central aggregation choice on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, comparing clean and robust accuracy under alternative averaging rules. v4 provided only a heuristic comparison of these rules. This substantially expands evidence about which component supplies robustness.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, across-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The retained reconstruction samples and EoT iterations are computational settings, not newly introduced uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports strong aggregation dependence: logit/probability averaging achieves robust accuracies of 0.0086/0.0092 on CIFAR-10 and 0.0436/0.0439 on CIFAR-100, with nearly unchanged clean accuracy. CARSO's corresponding 0.7613 and 0.6665 are retained from v4. With the comparator replacement, the CIFAR-10 best-AT entries change from 0.7107 to 0.7371 robust accuracy and from 0.9323 to 0.9368 clean accuracy.

T1.justification: The PGD and VAE definitions and derivations, aggregation equations, and logit inflation/deflation reasoning are retained. v4's Appendix D heuristic becomes v5's D.1; the added D.2 supplies empirical evidence rather than a new proof.

C1.justification: The central novelty and state-of-the-art robustness claims on the three main benchmarks remain. The revised title and contribution summary emphasize aggregation, but this component already belonged to the explicitly described CARSO pipeline in v4.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 changes the stated benefit of adversarial pretraining from improved clean accuracy to improved robust accuracy. Appendix D.2 interprets the new ablation as establishing aggregation's central role, while Section 5.3 newly acknowledges that its specific defensive mechanisms need further investigation.

D1.justification: Appendix E corrects the disclosed CIFAR-100 annealing duration from 250 to 150 epochs. The detailed layer specifications, other hyperparameters, hardware, training times, and implementation-access information are retained.

R1.justification: Bartoldson et al. (2024) is added to the introduction, related work, motivation, and best adversarial-training comparison. The earlier cited works and overall positioning against training-only and purification-only defenses remain.

P1.justification: v5 revises wording and terminology, updates the title, adopts author–year citations, adds a Broader Impact Statement, and subdivides Appendix D. Most prose and the main six-section and A–F appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: The document is extensively retypeset, changing typography, text width, title and author arrangement, and page headers. Existing tables are resized and repositioned, including decoder tables placed on separate pages, and the aggregation table is added. Figure 1's diagram is retained.

improvement.justification: The new controlled aggregation ablation strengthens a design choice supported only heuristically in v4, and the annealing correction makes the reported training budget internally consistent. These are useful improvements in evidence and reproducibility. The aggregation mechanism remains unresolved, and Appendix F retains an inconsistent attribution for the updated CIFAR-10 comparator.
